cause: R04 invalidated the epoch and dropped pending keys after navigation/process failure, but handed native consent and route delegates only the long-lived host cancellation token. These callbacks could keep working after page authority vanished; synchronous cancellation callbacks could also re-enter the bridge before revocation completed.
fix: A separate linked CancellationTokenSource is created for each admitted native request and bound to the document epoch. Every navigation/document/process transition increments epoch, copies and retires pending tokens, cancels them, and uses a depth guard to reject synchronous re-entry. The same per-request token is passed to consent and native route; finally disposes the lease. No new host.
